brief:
Small-scale farming projects are enabling Palestinians in Gaza to rebuild agricultural livelihoods following widespread devastation, Al Jazeera English reported. Farmers are using greenhouses and rented plots to grow crops despite extensive damage to land and infrastructure across the territory. The projects represent critical efforts to restore food production in areas where traditional farming systems have been severely disrupted.

The initiatives offer economic survival for agricultural workers whose communities face acute shortages of income and sustenance. Greenhouses provide controlled growing conditions while allowing farmers to work on limited available land, creating opportunities to generate revenue and grow food for their families. For many in Gaza, these small-scale operations have become lifelines in the face of ongoing hardship.
dek: Greenhouses and rented plots are lifelines for Gaza's farmers, helping them grow crops despite the extensive destruction.
title: Greenhouses help Gaza farmers resume crop production after destruction
